issues.description:
Method: Milkable.messageOnMilk
Problem statement: At the UML/interface section (problem_statement.md) the method is declared as messageOnMilk() with no parameters returning String. Later in the textual instructions (problem_statement.md) the same method is described as messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) taking a double parameter. Template: Main.java (template repository) calls messageOnMilk() with no arguments. Solution: Milkable.java (solution repository) defines messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch about the parameter list (no-arg vs. single double parameter) blocks students by making it unclear which signature to implement and can cause compilation failures or failing tests if they choose the wrong signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement text (line showing messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and its example) to describe a parameterless method messageOnMilk() returning String (for example: "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). This matches the UML, template usage, and solution. Alternatively (if the intent was to include milk volume), change the UML, template call sites (Main, Farm, tests) and the solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all implementations and calls accordingly. Prefer the first option to minimize changes to provided template and solution.

issues.description: Concept: the animal milking method. The problem statement's Part 2 text requires a method named messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (i.e., with a double parameter and a return that includes the volume). However the UML in the problem statement, the template code usage, and the solution all declare and use messageOnMilk() with no parameters. Specifically: problem statement Part 2 text calls it messageOnMilk(double milkVolume); the UML/interface diagram earlier shows messageOnMilk(): String (no parameter); the template Main.java calls milkable.messageOnMilk() with no argument; the solution defines interface Milkable.messageOnMilk() and implementations (Seal, Goat) with no parameter. This signature mismatch (parameter vs no-parameter) creates ambiguity for students which leads to compilation errors or incorrect implementations and test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the milk method signature consistent across all artifacts. The least disruptive fix is to update the problem statement Part 2 text to require messageOnMilk() with no parameter and adjust the example return string to match the existing code (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"). Alternatively, if the intention is to include a volume parameter, update the UML, template code (Main and Farm if applicable), solution interface and implementations to messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all calls and tests accordingly. Prefer aligning the textual requirement to the existing code (messageOnMilk() without parameters) unless tests/teaching intent explicitly require the volume parameter.
